To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Nigeria has a fractured structure and the future of the nation depends on the ability of the political leadership to address the fracture.
the structure of the Nigerian state is fractured, and credible elections cannot be held in such a fractured state.

there is no way a credible election can deliver good governance, political accountability and enable the Nigerian people fulfil their hopes and aspiration, as the desires of the majority of Nigerians are reflected in the demands of the various groups over the years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the future of Nigeria.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
credible elections in a fractured society cannot guarantee good governance and effective political accountability.
, credible elections in Nigeria can only be of any useful value in securing the future of Nigeria if the structure is transformed to meet the yearning and aspirations of Nigerians.
credible election is not enough for the future of Nigeria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, credible elections are important for the development of Nigeria, but the structure must be credible too.
the paper argues that the structure of Nigeria is in crisis, and that the crisis is not only in the structure but the structure itself has been fractured.

the structure of Nigeria has been fractured by the demands of the ethnic nationalities and the demands of the various ethnic groups for a Sovereign National Conference, and until this structure is fixed, no amount of credible election can deliver the desired good governance, effective accountability and political leadership in Nigeria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is need for a structural transformation of Nigeria before any election can be credible.
there is no way a credible election will take place in a country where the people are agitating for Sovereign National Conference and the country’s structure is fractured.
there is need for a new structure for Nigeria that addresses the demands of the ethnic nationalities and that will make the people feel a sense of belonging, security and ownership of the nation.
